detections.name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Elliptical spindle-shaped lesions with grayish center and dark reddish-brown margins
Coalescing spots causing leaf blade blighting
possible_causes: Relative humidity sustained >90% during tillering stage
Overuse of chemical urea nitrogen without balanced potassium
Microclimate fogging in high-density planted field
detections.management_immediate: Drain standing water for 48 hours to reduce canopy humidity. Stop all urea nitrogen top-dressing immediately.
detections.management_preventive: Adopt 20x15 cm seedling spacing and use blast-resistant seeds in future planting.
detections.management_biological: Apply foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens (0.2%) or Trichoderma viride culture early morning.
detections.management_ipm: Prophylactic Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6 g/L) only if lesions expand beyond 5% leaf area, adhering to regional safety norms.

xai_factors.description: Atmospheric moisture exceeds fungal spore germination threshold by 7%.
Persistent dew coating accelerates fungal germ tube penetration into leaf stomata.
Juvenile tender foliage provides ideal soft substrate for blast infection.
Waterlogged root zone limits systemic silica uptake needed for leaf cell wall rigidity.
Temperature is within the peak fungal metabolic multiplication range.

detections.counterfactual_tip: If relative humidity drops to 70% and stagnant water is drained, blast reproduction slows by ~62%.

detections.name: Tomato Early Blight
symptoms: Concentric target-board ring pattern on lower older foliage
Chlorotic bright yellow halo encircling necrotic spots
Defoliation of bottom leaves exposing fruit to sunscald
possible_causes: Soil splash carrying Alternaria solani fungal spores onto lower canopy
Heavy intermittent monsoon showers followed by warm afternoon sun
Lack of ground mulch allowing direct raindrop splatter
detections.management_immediate: Prune and safely burn or bury all diseased lower leaves up to 30cm height. Disinfect pruning shears between plants.
detections.management_preventive: Lay organic straw or silver reflective mulch to physically prevent soil splashing.
detections.management_biological: Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or 1% Bordeaux mixture to protect healthy upper foliage.
detections.management_ipm: Targeted Mancozeb 75 WP (2 g/L) protective barrier spray following authorized plant clinic guidelines.

xai_factors.description: Splash mechanics propelled dormant soil fungal inoculum onto basal leaves.
Warm daytime temperatures accelerate Alternaria conidial reproduction.
Poor lower canopy air circulation delayed foliage drying after rain.
Plant directs energy to fruits, decreasing natural phytoalexin defense in older leaves.
Adequate potassium maintains partial epidermal resistance.

detections.counterfactual_tip: Pruning bottom leaves and laying straw mulch reduces spore transmission probability by ~75%.

detections.name: Pink Bollworm
symptoms: Rosetted flower blooms failing to open properly
Small entry holes sealed with microscopic webbing on green bolls
Burrowing larvae feeding on immature seeds and lint inside boll segments
possible_causes: High nocturnal moth flight coinciding with peak boll formation stage
Survival of diapausing pupae from previous season crop residues
Delayed pest detection due to internal larval feeding habit
detections.management_immediate: Install 8 pheromone traps per acre immediately to monitor flight intensity. Remove and destroy rosetted flowers.
detections.management_preventive: Shred and bury all cotton stalks promptly post-harvest to break the diapausing overwintering cycle.
detections.management_biological: Release egg parasitoid wasps Trichogramma bactrae @ 60,000/ha weekly for 4 weeks.
detections.management_ipm: Time selective biorational insecticide sprays strictly within 48-72 hours of peak pheromone trap moth flushes.

xai_factors.description: Trap count exceeds the Economic Threshold Level for 3 consecutive days.
Tender green bolls provide high-protein seed food required by growing larvae.
Warm calm nights stimulate high mating and oviposition activity by female moths.
Neighboring untreated residue acted as a reservoir for pupal emergence.
Insufficient natural bio-predators allowed unrestrained larval hatching.

detections.counterfactual_tip: Deploying pheromone mating disruption and releasing Trichogramma wasps cuts boll infestation by ~68%.
